issues.detail: The source equation is C(gamma,x)=c(gamma,L) x ln(x)+b(gamma,L) x, with c and b obtained separately by fitting for each gamma and fit-window upper size L. The card AST instead uses L in place of x and fixes both fitted coefficients to 1, so it evaluates C=L ln(L)+L and has no dependence on gamma. Direct evaluation gives 24.635532333438686 at L=8 and 132.03592144986465 at L=30 for all gamma. No such curve or coefficient assignment is reported.

The frozen source supplies neither numeric c(gamma,L) and b(gamma,L) tables nor closed functions for them. Its finite-size-scaling expression contains an unspecified scaling function f. The quoted zeta, nu, and gamma_c determine scaling variables and critical behavior, not the amplitude C at a requested control point. Therefore the selected controls cannot objectively determine a central-value C response.

In the source, x is the size coordinate varied within [8,L], while L labels the upper end of each fit window and reaches 30. The card removes x, exposes L as the sole size argument, assigns it the interval [8,30], and calls this integer linear lattice size continuous. Its gamma interval [0.1,0.4] is also unsupported as a closed response domain: the paper states a point at 0.1J and area-law behavior for gamma>=0.4J, not that 0.4J is a maximum. These domain choices would admit queries for which the paper gives no defined pointwise output.

The card stores c_log_coefficient=1 and b_area_coefficient=1 while its own roles acknowledge that both are fit-derived functions rather than fixed constants. Line 241 gives only their symbolic roles; it does not anchor either value to 1. The additional V_coupling_prefactor=1 record is an unnecessary algebraic placeholder rather than a reported fitted parameter. These records cannot be used as source truth.

The ScienceCard contains one claim and no two disjoint branch-specific condition sets. The logarithmic-law point at gamma=0.1J and area-law regime for gamma>=0.4J are outcomes along the same proposed public gamma control, not two hidden mechanisms or conditions with the same public controls and readout. The source does not provide a second pointwise numeric law under a distinct private condition, so Historical and alternate branches cannot share a valid Identification skeleton without adding an unstated world.

The source quotes plus/minus values for the FSS estimates but does not define their uncertainty convention. The card correctly records this as a source ambiguity attached to the selected claim, control, readout, mechanism, and fit condition. An eligible selection could not silently discard that unresolved provenance; in this case it is secondary to the missing executable response and branch pair.
